questions.q: How many sides does a standard red stop sign have?
questions.a: Eight. Count them around the edge.

questions.q: What is the mathematical name for that eight-sided shape?
questions.a: An octagon. Its name starts with the same prefix as octopus.

questions.q: Which direction is opposite east on a compass?
questions.a: West. East and west sit across from each other.

questions.q: If the top of a map is north, which direction is the left edge?
questions.a: West. Turn the map to face the same way as your compass to check.

questions.q: What do you call a road that goes underneath a mountain?
questions.a: A tunnel. The mountain stays above you.

questions.q: What do you call the part of a bridge that crosses the gap between two supports?
questions.a: A span. A long bridge can have several spans.

questions.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
questions.a: Thirty. Half of 60 is 30.

questions.q: A trip takes 90 minutes. If you leave at 2:15, when do you arrive in the same time zone?
questions.a: 3:45. Add one hour, then another 30 minutes.

questions.q: What is the book of maps in a glove compartment called?
questions.a: An atlas. It can hold road maps for a whole country.

questions.q: On a map, 1 centimetre stands for 5 kilometres. How far apart are towns drawn 3 centimetres apart?
questions.a: 15 kilometres. Multiply the map distance by five.

questions.q: What is the name of a river that flows into a larger river?
questions.a: A tributary. Follow it downstream and it joins the larger river.

questions.q: What do we call the point where two rivers meet?
questions.a: A confluence. Look for a Y shape on a map.

questions.q: Which bright object lights the Moon?
questions.a: The Sun. Moonlight is reflected sunlight.

questions.q: Why does the Moon sometimes look like a crescent?
questions.a: From Earth we see only part of its sunlit half. The amount we see changes as the Moon orbits Earth.

questions.q: What is a group of sheep in a field called?
questions.a: A flock. Farmers also use the word for a group of birds.

questions.q: What is the word for a mammal that eats plants?
questions.a: A herbivore. Sheep and cows are examples.

questions.q: What has to hit raindrops for you to see a daytime rainbow?
questions.a: Sunlight. A shower with the Sun behind you is a good time to look.

questions.q: Why do two passengers see a flash of lightning before they hear its thunder?
questions.a: Light travels faster than sound. Both come from the same lightning event.

questions.q: What do we call land surrounded by water on all sides?
questions.a: An island. It can be in a lake, river or ocean.

questions.q: What do we call land surrounded by water on three sides?
questions.a: A peninsula. One side connects it to the mainland.

questions.q: Which city is home to the Eiffel Tower?
questions.a: Paris, in France.

questions.q: Which river runs through Paris past the Eiffel Tower?
questions.a: The Seine. It flows through the city towards the English Channel.

questions.q: Which country has a mainland shaped like a boot?
questions.a: Italy. Its toe points towards Sicily.

questions.q: Which is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.a: Sicily. It sits just off the toe of Italy.

questions.q: In which US state would you visit the Grand Canyon?
questions.a: Arizona. The national park is in the northern part of the state.

questions.q: Which river flows through the Grand Canyon?
questions.a: The Colorado River. You can see it from some viewpoints on the rim.

questions.q: Which Australian city has an opera house shaped like white sails?
questions.a: Sydney. The building stands beside Sydney Harbour.

questions.q: Which city is the capital of Australia?
questions.a: Canberra. Sydney is the capital of the state of New South Wales.

questions.q: On which continent would you visit the pyramids of Giza?
questions.a: Africa. The pyramids stand in Egypt.

questions.q: Which sea would you reach by following the Nile River downstream to its delta?
questions.a: The Mediterranean Sea. The river reaches it on the northern coast of Egypt.
